details: Echoes of Orbit: The Forgotten Explorers Echoes of Orbit is a documentary-style educational project that explores the forgotten history of human space exploration. It focuses on abandoned spacecraft, retired rovers, lunar landers, astronaut equipment and the remnants of missions across the Moon, Mars and asteroids. The project explains how these machines were designed, how they worked, what scientific discoveries they contributed to and why they were left behind after their missions ended. It highlights important explorers such as the Apollo Lunar Module, Moon Buggies, Lunokhod rovers, Mars rovers, Hayabusa and OSIRIS-REx. The main goal is to raise awareness about the history of space exploration and the importance of understanding what happens to spacecraft after their missions are completed. It also highlights issues such as space debris, planetary protection and the responsibility of preserving extraterrestrial environments. This project benefits students, space enthusiasts and the general public by making complex space exploration history more understandable and engaging. It encourages scientific curiosity, environmental awareness and interest in future space research. The project uses research from reliable space organizations and scientific sources, including NASA, JAXA and ESA. Information is presented through organized explanations, historical timelines and astronomy-inspired visual designs. Its creativity comes from presenting space exploration from a different perspective: instead of focusing only on successful launches and discoveries, it tells the stories of the machines and equipment humanity left behind. It connects science, history, technology and environmental responsibility to show that every space mission leaves a lasting mark.
